```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

**Status: EXPLORATORY.** Not in the pre-specified confirmatory set; every p-value and CI is
unadjusted.

**Question.** With the corrected fava weights (see `16_Fava_Neighbor`), the one fava result is
that fava is heavier next to inoculated wheat under severe drought (~3.7 g) than in any other
intercrop cell (~2 g). Does the pot-level allocation to fava, or wheat's allocation to berries,
track wheat's AMF colonization as a continuous variable?

**Definitions (confirmed with Celeste, Nov 2026).**

* Allocation to fava = fava share of pot NPP, `fava_pct_pot` = `Fava_g / Pot_NPP_g` (= `Pot_pcent_fava`).
* Allocation to berries = wheat berry mass / wheat NPP, `berry_alloc`.
* AMF colonization = wheat root total (hyphal) colonization, `hyphal`. Arbuscules (`arb_pct`) in the supplement.
  Fava roots were not stained, so this is always *wheat's* colonization.
* Data: the 30 intercrop pots only. Color/fill = wheat inoculation (inoculated #CC5500 filled, solid;
  sterile slate blue open, dashed, from `fig_style.R`); panels = water level.

**Caveat on the sterile pots.** Colonization in sterile pots is low (mostly near background), so
a slope fitted within sterile pots is a weak test. Inoculated pots under moderate and severe drought
also span a very narrow range (about 0.9 to 1.0), so a within-cell slope there is barely estimable.
See the colonization-range table below before reading anything into the lines.

```{r libs}
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(patchwork)
source("../fig_style.R")

inter <- readRDS("../wheat_audited.rds") %>% filter(Poly == "Inter") %>%
  mutate(fava_share = fava_pct_pot * 100, berry_pct = berry_alloc * 100,
         hyph_pct = hyphal * 100, arb = arb_pct * 100, fava = Fava_g, wheat = W_NPP)
stopifnot(nrow(inter) == 30, all(table(inter$Inoc, inter$Water) == 5),
          isTRUE(all.equal(inter$fava_pct_pot, inter$Fava_g / inter$Pot_NPP_g, tolerance = 1e-4)))
```

# Colonization range in each cell

```{r range}
inter %>% group_by(Water, Inoc) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), `hyphal mean (%)` = mean(hyph_pct), `min` = min(hyph_pct), `max` = max(hyph_pct),
            `arbuscules mean (%)` = mean(arb), `fava share (%)` = mean(fava_share),
            `fava (g)` = mean(fava), `wheat NPP (g)` = mean(wheat),
            `berry alloc (%)` = mean(berry_pct), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Cell means, intercrop pots (n = 5 per cell)")
```

# Figure: allocation against colonization

```{r fig-main, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6.5}
alloc_panel <- function(dat, x, y, ylab, xlab, strips = TRUE) {
  ggplot(dat, aes({{ x }}, {{ y }}, colour = Inoc, fill = Inoc, shape = Inoc, linetype = Inoc)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_point(size = 2.4, stroke = 0.9) +
    facet_wrap(~ Water, nrow = 1, labeller = labeller(Water = water_lab)) +
    inoc_scales() +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab) +
    theme_fig() +
    if (!strips) theme(strip.text = element_blank()) else NULL
}

p_fava  <- alloc_panel(inter, hyph_pct, fava_share, "Fava share of pot NPP (%)", NULL)
p_berry <- alloc_panel(inter, hyph_pct, berry_pct, "Wheat berry allocation (%)",
                       "Wheat root AMF colonization (%)", strips = FALSE)
fig <- (p_fava / p_berry) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
fig
ggsave("figures/Fig21_Alloc_vs_Colonization.pdf", fig, width = 9, height = 6.5)
```

# Slopes against colonization (EXPLORATORY)

One model per response, fitted once on all 30 pots: `y ~ hyphal * Water * Inoc`, with slopes
per Inoc x Water cell from `emtrends`. Slopes are per 10 percentage points of colonization.
Read the cells with a narrow x range (see table above) as uninformative regardless of p.

```{r slopes}
slope_tab <- function(resp) {
  m <- lm(reformulate("hyph_pct * Water * Inoc", resp), data = inter)
  emtrends(m, ~ Inoc | Water, var = "hyph_pct") %>% summary(infer = TRUE) %>% as_tibble() %>%
    transmute(response = resp, Water, Inoc,
              slope_per10 = hyph_pct.trend * 10, lo = lower.CL * 10, hi = upper.CL * 10, p = p.value)
}
slopes <- bind_rows(slope_tab("fava_share"), slope_tab("berry_pct"))
knitr::kable(slopes %>% mutate(across(c(slope_per10, lo, hi), ~ round(.x, 2)), p = signif(p, 2)),
             col.names = c("Response", "Water", "Inoc", "Slope per 10 pts", "95% lo", "95% hi", "p"))
```

# What the fava share is made of

The fava share can rise because fava gets heavier or because wheat gets lighter. This splits the
severe-drought cell into its two pieces.

```{r fava-parts, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6.5}
p_fg <- alloc_panel(inter, hyph_pct, fava, "Fava biomass (g per pot)", NULL)
p_wg <- alloc_panel(inter, hyph_pct, wheat, "Wheat NPP (g per pot, 6 plants)",
                    "Wheat root AMF colonization (%)", strips = FALSE)
fig_parts <- (p_fg / p_wg) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
fig_parts
ggsave("figures/Fig21S_FavaWheat_vs_Colonization.pdf", fig_parts, width = 9, height = 6.5)
```

# Supplement: arbuscules on the x axis

```{r fig-arb, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6.5}
p_fava_a  <- alloc_panel(inter, arb, fava_share, "Fava share of pot NPP (%)", NULL)
p_berry_a <- alloc_panel(inter, arb, berry_pct, "Wheat berry allocation (%)",
                         "Wheat root arbuscule colonization (%)", strips = FALSE)
fig_arb <- (p_fava_a / p_berry_a) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
fig_arb
ggsave("figures/Fig21S_Alloc_vs_Arbuscules.pdf", fig_arb, width = 9, height = 6.5)
```
